review.translation: [And the fear of you|0] [and the dread of you|1] [will be|2] [on|3] [every|4] [wild animal of|5] [the land|6] [and on|7] [every|8] [bird of|9] [the sky|10], [on everything|11] [that|12] [the ground|14] [teems with|13], [and on all|15] [the fish of|16] [the sea|17]. [Into your hand|18] [they have been given|19].

analysis.evidence: וּמוֹרַאֲכֶם is paired with וְחִתְּכֶם, “and the dread of you.” The verse says this fear will be upon the animals, so they experience it and the people addressed are its object.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and.” The masculine singular noun מוֹרָא is in the construct state with the second-person masculine plural suffix כֶם, which identifies the people whom the animals fear.

draft.change: Create the חתת root article with the masculine noun חַת and its sense of dread.
draft.definition: חַת is dread inspired by someone.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 9:2 the dread of Noah and his sons is paired with the fear of them and is said to come upon the animals.

analysis.evidence: וְחִתְּכֶם stands beside וּמוֹרַאֲכֶם, “the fear of you.” Both nouns share יִהְיֶה עַל, “will be upon,” which identifies the animals as those who experience the fear and dread. The parallel rules out the source gloss “watering-trough.”
analysis.morphology: וְ is the conjunction “and.” חִתְּ is the masculine singular construct form of חַת before the second-person masculine plural suffix כֶם, which refers to Noah and his sons.
analysis.sense: Dread that the animals feel toward Noah and his sons.

analysis.evidence: יִהְיֶה links וּמוֹרַאֲכֶם וְחִתְּכֶם (“the fear and dread of you”) to עַל (“upon”). God tells Noah and his sons that this fear and dread will be upon every beast of the earth and every bird of the sky.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine singular, with prospective force.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.morphology: Preposition without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עַל כָּל חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ, כָּל extends the stated fear and dread to every beast of the earth. The parallel וְעַל כָּל עוֹף הַשָּׁמָיִם applies the same wording to every bird of the heavens.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, governing חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 66318:13, 66305:4, 66068:8, 66067:6, 65822:1, 65817:3.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: wild beast, beast of the field

analysis.evidence: The verse groups creatures by habitat. חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ names the wild animals of the land alongside עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם, the birds of the sky, and דְּגֵי הַיָּם, the fish of the sea.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ precedes a singular absolute noun of common gender. הָאָרֶץ completes the construct phrase חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ.

analysis.evidence: The verse says that fear and dread of the addressees will be upon every beast of the earth. וְעַל repeats the preposition to extend the same statement to every bird of the heavens.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and.” The preposition עַל means “upon” and governs כָּל עוֹף הַשָּׁמָיִם, “every bird of the heavens.”

analysis.evidence: In וְעַל כָּל עוֹף הַשָּׁמָיִם, כָּל extends the scope of the fear and dread to every bird of the heavens, just as the preceding phrase includes every beast of the earth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state before עוֹף הַשָּׁמָיִם.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67351:14, 67079:16, 66067:10, 65822:4.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67586:4, 67586:8, 67347:13, 67089:16, 67079:17, 65812:14, 65809:4.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with the prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: In בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תִּרְמֹשׂ הָאֲדָמָה, כֹל stands on its own as the antecedent of אֲשֶׁר. The relative clause specifies what “everything” includes here: everything that moves on the ground.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition בְּ governs כֹל, a masculine singular absolute noun.
Indeclinable relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תִּרְמֹשׂ הָאֲדָמָה, הָאֲדָמָה is the subject. The phrase means “all that the ground teems with,” referring to creatures that move about on it.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third-person feminine singular, agreeing with הָאֲדָמָה.

analysis.evidence: In בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תִּרְמֹשׂ הָאֲדָמָה, the ground is the surface on which creatures crawl, alongside the sky for birds and the sea for fish.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a feminine singular common noun in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: the ground underfoot; the face of the earth

analysis.evidence: In וּבְכָל דְּגֵי הַיָּם, כָל takes the definite plural phrase ‘the fish of the sea’ as its complement and includes the entire group among the creatures subject to human dread.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ ‘and’ and the preposition בְּ precede כָל, a masculine singular construct noun governing דְּגֵי הַיָּם ‘the fish of the sea’.

analysis.evidence: In וּבְכָל דְּגֵי הַיָּם, “and all the fish of the sea,” the construct plural דְּגֵי takes הַיָּם as its complement. The phrase names sea creatures alongside the land animals and birds.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 65820:14, 65818:8.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ + masculine singular absolute common noun.

draft.change: Link the occurrence to word 0 of yd and clarify its existing Genesis 9:2 evidence note with the Hebrew clause.
draft.definition: To give something into someone’s hand is to place it under that person’s control.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:2 uses בְּיֶדְכֶם with נִתָּנוּ for the transfer of the creatures into human control. The Hebrew sense hand-power already cites this verse as defining evidence.

analysis.evidence: בְּיֶדְכֶם נִתָּנוּ means “into your hand they have been given.” The plural verb refers back to the creatures of land, sky, and sea. Giving them into the addressees’ hand places them under their control.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ introduces the singular construct form of יָד, a common noun tagged for both genders. The second-person masculine plural suffix כֶם supplies the possessor, “your.”
analysis.sense: power or control over what is given into someone’s hand

analysis.evidence: בְּיֶדְכֶם נִתָּנוּ means “into your hand they have been given.” The plural verb refers to the creatures just listed, and “into your hand” expresses the authority granted to Noah and his sons over them.
analysis.morphology: Niphal perfect, third person common plural. The ending ־וּ marks the plural subject.
analysis.sense: be given into another’s hand or power
